lots.guide_summary: All evidence is Gowans Hobart hammer prices in AUD, buyer's premium extra. Six same-type Baluchi sales of 170-220 cm length sold at $120-300 hammer (Sep 2025 to Sep 2026), median about $265. One same rug passed in twice before selling at $300. Category guides (Afghan Turkman/Ashak/Balouchi of other sizes) run $100-260, with room-size Turkman to $410-460. No asking prices. Rate 1.0, all AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving same-type SOLD in last 24 months = $120 hammer (Gowans 419656, Persian Baluchi 214x111, Jun 2026) / 1.22 = $98.36, rounded down to $95. Flip: likely resale about $200 hammer (lower half of the $120-300 same-type range, as Hobart rug sales are erratic and some need relisting), less about 15% seller commission and fees (assumed, $30) and $0 postage (local auction resale) = $170 net; $170 / 2.44 = $69.67, rounded down to $65. Flip margin is thin; best as a keep.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of type and size from the lot text and photos, many same-room SOLD entries opened, but no maker mark to read and condition (pile wear, moth, stains, back) cannot be judged from cut-out photos.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All researcher lot ids, sizes, bid counts and sale prices confirmed in the Gowans API JSON. Re-labelled Afghan Turkman/Balouchi of different size as category guide (as the researcher did). The two room-size Turkman sales ($410, $460) are kept out of the guide range as they are far larger. Note: URLs are API search URLs, the lot id identifies the record.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three studio cut-out photos. Classic Baluch layout: three stepped medallions on navy field, white accent motifs, multiple stepped borders. Pile looks even and full, colours strong, no visible holes or stains; fringe short and even at one end. No label or back photo.
lots.condition: Appears good from photos; back, pile depth, moth and sides not visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the back of the rug (knot count, any repairs), any moth or worn patches, and both fringes and side cords intact? What is the 'documentation of authenticity' (dealer certificate)?

lots.guide_summary: Two same-district Hamadan sales at Gowans, both smaller than this rug, sold at $170 and $180 hammer (May 2026). A rug twice the size made $330 (category guide). All sold, AUD, premium extra; no unsold or asking evidence. Rate 1.0.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD in last 24 months = $170 hammer (Gowans 411523, Hamadan 150x82, May 2026) / 1.22 = $139.34, rounded down to $135. Flip: likely resale about $180 hammer (this rug is larger than the comps, but evidence is only two sales), less about 15% seller commission and fees (assumed, $27) and $0 postage = $153 net; $153 / 2.44 = $62.70, rounded down to $60.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification clear from the lot text and photos, two close same-room SOLD entries opened, but both are smaller rugs, 'Enjelas' itself has no direct sold match, and condition cannot be judged from cut-out photos.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's fourth entry (an aggregate '$180 and $150-190 range' of Mashwani, Baluchi and Somak rugs): it bundles several different weaves, Somak is flat-woven, and the '$150-190' figure is not a single sale. The underlying sales are real (419652 $160, 419656 $120, 422873 $120, 424505 $120) but are not the same item. Kept $330 Hamadan only as a category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three studio cut-out photos. Cream field reads clean and bright, pile looks even, colours fresh; white fringe present at one end, slightly ragged but intact. No back or label photo.
lots.condition: Appears good from photos; back, moth and sides not visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the back (any repairs or reweaves), moth or worn patches, whether the cream field has stains, and that both fringes and side cords are intact?

lots.what_it_is: Large abstract painting by Ryllton Viney (Launceston artist; named in the lot title), 'An Impenetrable Wall II', 2011, oil and Florentine medium on canvas, from the suite 'Enclose/Disclose' (per the handwritten back label). H 137 x W 122 cm, unframed. Dark, heavily textured monochrome surface.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: no sold, unsold or asking evidence found for Ryllton Viney at Armitage, Gowans (API search returns only vineyard wine lots), or the open web. AASD and Artrecord are bot-walled. The market for his work appears very shallow.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are $0. Any bid would be a personal-taste decision, not a market-backed one.
lots.confidence_reason: Artist is named in the lot title and the back label matches his 'Enclose/Disclose' exhibition, but no signature is visible in the photos, the label is a handwritten sheet of paper, and there is no price evidence at all.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher gave no entries. Verifier WebSearches (site:armitage.bidsonline.com.au Ryllton Viney; Ryllton/Rylton Viney painting sold) and a Gowans API search for viney/rylton/ryllton found nothing usable. Wayne Viney (printmaker) results are a different artist and were not used.
lots.key_photo_findings: Front: dark brown/black textured abstract with horizontal bands, stippled and incised marks; enlarged lower edge shows no visible signature. Back: handwritten paper label taped on stretcher bar, torn at one corner, reading 'An Impenetrable Wall II, 2011. Oil and Florentine medium on canvas. From the suite Enclose/Disclose'. No artist name on the label. Lot text says 'An Impenetrable Wall' and 'mixed media', a minor mismatch with the label (II, oil).
lots.condition: Surface looks intact in the photos; edges and back only partly visible. Unframed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the painting signed anywhere (front, side edge or verso)? Is there any gallery label (Gallery Pejean) or provenance with it? Any cracking, flaking or damage to the heavy textured surface or canvas edges?
